bbo.reasoning_excerpt:
The user wants a JSON verdict on whether MER, MCS, UWEC are effective linguistic measures for MALI13 (bbo, Northern Bobo Madaré) given the 300-sentence stress audit and Lean 4 hardening theorems.

Key data:
- Clean strict parse only 40.89% (low), EMPR 8.27%, diacritic words 31.81%
- Cohen's d: MER_corrupt=17.05 (huge), MCS_shift=6.42 (large), UWEC_ood=0.36 (negligible)
- OOD strict-parse gap only 0.22 pp (tiny)
- Shift MCS recovery 54.5 pp; MER>1 saturation prevented 100%; truncation bias 51.9 pp
- 6-regime matrix shows MER raw hits >1 in overgeneration (1.14, 100% >1), MCS aligned recovers shift (0.9359) but index/corpus collapse (0.39), UWEC orig vs inv differ (0.5766 vs 0.5983 clean; 0.371 vs 0.9298 overgeneration — inversion matters)
- Lean theorems: bounded MER always unit-bounded (so raw MER can exceed 1 but bounded version capped), MCS shift collapse witness (mcsMatches=0 under shift), stageLcs resists shift (LCS=4 while MCS=0), corpus denom asymmetry, MER overgen >1 witness.

Deduction: MER is effective for corruption detection (huge effect size) but needs bounding (bounded_mer_always_unit_bounded) to avoid >1 saturation; raw MER saturates in overgeneration. MCS is effective for shift recovery only in aligned mode (54.5 pp recovery, aligned 0.9359) but collapses under index/corpus modes (Lean witness mcs_shift_collapse_witness) and has denominator asymmetry — needs aligned-index hardening. UWEC shows negligible OOD discrimination (d=0.36) and only modest regime sensitivity; inversion (uwec_inv) matters in overgeneration (0.9298 vs 0.371) — mixed, needs inversion-aware hardening. Overall: EFFECTIVE_WITH_HARDENING. Score maybe ~72.
